documents.title: 2026–27 Registration & Records Handbook
documents.summary: Enrollment changes, records, transcripts, and privacy.

sections.heading: Add and drop dates
sections.text: Students may add a full-term course through the seventh calendar day of the term and drop it without a transcript notation through the fourteenth calendar day. After day 14, the withdrawal process applies.

sections.heading: Course withdrawal
sections.text: A full-term course withdrawal submitted from day 15 through the end of week 10 receives a W notation. Requests after week 10 require a documented extraordinary-circumstances petition to the academic dean.

sections.heading: Official transcripts
sections.text: Current students request an official transcript through the student portal. Standard electronic delivery has no college processing fee; third-party delivery services may charge their own fee.

documents.title: Student Financial Aid Guide 2026–27
documents.summary: Aid eligibility, disbursement, satisfactory progress, and withdrawals.

sections.heading: Enrollment and disbursement
sections.text: Institutional grants are initially calculated using enrolled credits at the census date. Institutional scholarships are credited no earlier than 10 days before the first day of classes, subject to completed document verification and eligibility.

sections.heading: Satisfactory academic progress
sections.text: Undergraduates must complete at least 67 percent of attempted credits and maintain the cumulative GPA required for their class level. Progress is reviewed after each spring term; students may appeal a suspension with documentation.

sections.heading: Withdrawal and aid return
sections.text: Withdrawing from every course may require recalculation and return of financial aid. The amount depends on the withdrawal date and aid type, so students must request an individual estimate from Student Financial Services.

documents.title: Residence Life Community Standards 2026–27
documents.summary: Residential conduct, guests, safety, and room changes.

sections.heading: Overnight guests
sections.text: A resident may host the same overnight guest for no more than two consecutive nights and six nights in a calendar month. All roommates must consent, and the guest must register at the service desk.

sections.heading: Room changes
sections.text: Residents request room changes in the housing portal. Except for urgent safety situations, no moves occur during the first two weeks of a term while occupancy is verified.

sections.heading: Quiet hours
sections.text: Quiet hours are 10 p.m. to 8 a.m. Sunday through Thursday and midnight to 9 a.m. Friday and Saturday. Courtesy hours apply at all times.

sections.heading: Overnight guests
sections.text: A resident may host an overnight guest for up to three consecutive nights and eight nights in a calendar month with roommate consent.

documents.title: Campus Technology & Account Standard
documents.summary: Accounts, wireless access, passwords, and acceptable use.

sections.heading: Wireless network access
sections.text: Students connect personal devices to GLSIT-Secure using their campus username and password. GLSIT-Guest is intended for visitors and does not provide access to library-licensed resources.

sections.heading: Password reset
sections.text: Students may reset a forgotten password at accounts.gls-demo.invalid after completing multifactor verification. If verification is unavailable, the Technology Support Center requires photo identification during an in-person or video appointment.

sections.heading: Acceptable use
sections.text: Campus systems may not be used to distribute malware, evade access controls, harass others, or infringe copyright. Suspected compromises should be reported promptly to the Technology Support Center.

documents.title: Student Conduct Code 2026–27
documents.summary: Academic integrity, conduct process, sanctions, and appeals.

sections.heading: Academic integrity
sections.text: Academic misconduct includes unauthorized collaboration, presenting another person’s work as one’s own, fabricating evidence, or using prohibited resources during an assessment. Instructors must identify permitted collaboration and tools in course materials.

sections.heading: Conduct meeting and notice
sections.text: A student receives written notice of the alleged conduct and a meeting opportunity. The student may bring one support person, who may advise but may not speak on the student’s behalf.

sections.heading: Appeals
sections.text: A conduct outcome may be appealed within seven business days for a material procedural error, significant new information, or a sanction claimed to be disproportionate. The appeal must explain the specific ground.
